decision.summary: Amelia Clarke's email is a duplicate report of the already-booked routine job R-4801, so no new ticket was created. I told her it is on R-4801 with the 15 Oct 08:00-12:00 visit, added her update to the ticket, and flagged the worsening drip to Swift Plumbing & Heating. My tenant email wrongly referred to an out-of-hours line with no number on file, and my first ticket note said the provider had been asked when it had not; I corrected the note.

answers.question: 1. Should a new repair job be created?
answers.answer: No. R-4801 is already open for the same dripping kitchen tap at P-201, at visit stage with Swift Plumbing & Heating on 15 Oct 2026 08:00-12:00. The tenant's email is an update on that fault, so it is linked to R-4801 rather than duplicated.

answers.question: 2. What do you reply to the tenant?
answers.answer: Sent email MSG-101 (ledger A2): her report is on existing job R-4801, the booked visit on record is Thu 15 Oct 2026 08:00-12:00, her update about the constant drip has been added, and she should reply if it gets worse. Caveat: it refers to an out-of-hours line, but no number is on file, so none was given; this is a wording flaw to note.

answers.question: 3. What, if anything, do you change on existing records?
answers.answer: Added a note to R-4801 with the tenant's report and the visit on record (ledger A1). Corrected the note (ledger A4) because it wrongly said the provider had been asked. Did not change the stage, visit, severity or contractor. Sent the provider an SMS (MSG-102, ledger A3) flagging the worsening fault. Scheduled a review for 2026-10-16 (ledger A5).

conflicts: Tenant email says the tap is worsening; R-4801 description and severity still say routine dripping tap. Trusted the current record for the job and the tenant's latest report for the change in condition; no severity change made.
My tenant email mentioned an out-of-hours line with no number on file; this is an error in my message, not a conflict in records.

args.body:
Hello Amelia,

Thank you for letting us know the kitchen tap is getting worse. We already have a repair booked for this, so we have not opened a new one. Your existing job is R-4801.

Our records show a visit on Thursday 15 October 2026, between 08:00 and 12:00, with our plumber Swift Plumbing & Heating. We have added your update to the job so they know it is now dripping constantly, even when fully closed.

If the tap gets much worse before then, or you have any water running that you cannot stop, please reply here and we will look at it again straight away. If it is a flood or you cannot turn the water off, please call us on the out-of-hours line and turn off the isolation valve under the sink if you can reach it safely.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings
